title: A busy link. A working factory.
profile_note: Historical RFC 4594 Example 3. RFC 8622 replaces CS1 with LE for current lower-effort recommendations.

beats.title: Read the lid
beats.caption: A crate is one packet. Six lights carry its DSCP label; two separate lights carry ECN.

beats.title: Find the application
beats.caption: The access sorter reads the application label to choose a service lane.

beats.title: Choose a trustworthy label
beats.caption: The paint booth replaces an untrusted label with EF for this voice packet. Its ECN bits stay unchanged.

beats.title: Keep the promise small
beats.caption: The token tank admits the contracted voice packet and limits excess traffic before the priority queue.

beats.title: Wait in a real queue
beats.caption: A buffer holds packets until the scheduler has room. The trace records each wait.

beats.title: Share the output
beats.caption: The priority lane goes first; weighted lanes share the capacity left over.

beats.title: One hop complete
beats.caption: Our voice packet reaches the output. The remaining factory keeps serving other classes.

beats.title: Make congestion visible
beats.caption: AF packets with higher drop precedence meet earlier Spillway thresholds. Drops and deliveries remain visible in the dashboard.

beats.title: The whole factory
beats.caption: Nine service classes share one connection in this historical RFC 4594 example. Each route is a real compiled datapath.

beats.title: Every crate accounted for
beats.caption: The arrival trace has drained. Inspect the totals, replay a beat, or return to the beginner campaign.
